title: Max Dowman Obliterates Jude Bellingham Record—but Bigger Honor Out of Reach
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom6:35 AM ESTIt was a night to savor for Max Dowman. / MB Media/Getty ImagesMax Dowman became the first 16-year-old to ever appear for England men’s U-21 team on Friday night, surpassing a certain Jude Bellingham as the youngest player to represent the young lions. Yet, it wasn’t an entirely positive evening.

Arsenal’s teenage star has enjoyed the sort of prodigious rise reserved for comic book characters. A member of England’s U-16s when he was just 14, the youngest Premier League winner ever had jumped up to the international U-19s by the time he was 15.

After impressing Ben Futcher during the elongated fall internationals—despite receiving a red card which would serve as a warning for some hot-headed behavior at club level—Dowman earned a call-up to Lee Carsley’s U-21s this month.

Dowman was introduced for the final half-hour as part of a quintuple substitution during Friday’s friendly against Portugal at Bristol City’s Ashton Gate home. The mass changes couldn’t alter the scoreline, which would end 1–0 in favor of the visitors, but Carsley was impressed by the Arsenal gem.

Jude Bellingham didn’t spend long with the U-21s. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesMax Dowman—16 years and 317 days (2026)Jude Bellingham—17 years and 70 days (2020)Theo Walcott—17 years and 152 days (2006)Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain—17 years and 177 days (2011)Joe Mattock—17 years and 185 days (2007)Data via Transfermarkt.

“I thought he was outstanding when he came on tonight,” the manager gushed. “I thought all of the subs made a real impact. I thought Max was unlucky not to get an assist, he made a great pass to Mikey Moore.
“He took up some really good positions, both in the 10 and out wide, he’s got a big future ahead.”

England will be at the U-21 European Championship this coming summer looking to defend a title the nation won in 2025 and 2023. With another friendly to come against France on Monday followed by March’s fixtures, there is only a small window in which Dowman can prove his worth to Carsley.

“We’ve only got three games left before the Euros,” the former senior England interim manager warned. “So it’s important that he puts himself in the shop window to be on the plane. It’s important that he keeps playing well, getting minutes, showing a really good attitude, like he has done.”

Yet, the fact that Dowman’s focus should be on the U-21s rather than the senior side has already effectively robbed him of the chance for even greater glory; namely, breaking more records for the senior national team.
Max Dowman comes on to make his England U21s debut, making history as the youngest-ever player. Hell of a reception for the 16-year-old here at Ashton Gate. pic.twitter.com/xo77qtlEj1

Dowman is already the youngest player to start in the Premier League or feature for England’s U-17s and U-19s. No one can match his debut at Champions League level while he also became the youngest goalscorer in the Premier League era last season. Yet, unless Thomas Tuchel has a sudden change of heart this month, he won’t become the youngest England senior men’s international.

Even if Dowman is unexpectedly picked by Tuchel for England’s next fixtures in March, the teenager born on New Year’s Eve will have aged out of contention to supplant Theo Walcott’s record of 17 years and 75 days.
Should England’s Nations League quarterfinal first leg be schedule on March 25, Dowman would be 17 years and 84 days young, enough to nudge him into second place in the record books.
Data via England. Correct as of Nov. 14, 2026.

In truth, this statistical wrinkle will likely be of little consequence to Dowman. As Carsley pointed out, his first focus should be on cementing his place as a regular for the U-21s ahead of a tournament which would prepare him for what a summer as a senior international may look like in the future.

England men could feasibly qualify for the Nations League finals in June, with a single-legged semifinal and final taking place after the club campaign’s conclusion. Should Dowman even be under consideration, he may be better served heading off to Albania and Serbia for the U-21 Euros where he could get more playing time rather than sitting on the bench in what remains a competition of dubious importance.
In any case, there will be plenty more records for Dowman to break in the coming years.
